references.text: The strategic distance of three days in 30:36 sets the context for Laban's reaction and Jacob's flight, which occurs 'on the third day' in 31:22.
The verses mark respectively the beginning (29:10) and the end (30:36) of the period when Jacob tended Laban's small livestock.
The literal shepherding of Laban's flock (30:36) serves as an earthly parallel to God's spiritual guidance of 'Jacob' in Psalm 78.
A clear thematic parallel: Both Jacob and Moses must first serve as shepherds for a father-in-law before becoming leaders of God's people.
The verses are directly connected parts of the same strategy: 30:36 describes the geographical separation, while 30:42 describes the selective method.
